md-baltimore-city-2026-boe-atlarge-day-j.name: Jamar Day
md-baltimore-city-2026-boe-atlarge-day-j.bio: Former teacher and dean of students in Baltimore City and DC public schools; special assistant at the Maryland Department of General Services.

positions.stance: Supports publicly defined performance metrics for district leadership and regular public reporting on district progress.
Wants to audit non-instructional duties, add workload indicators to administrator evaluations, and expand mental health supports for school staff.
Proposes reviewing district-mandated assessments and reducing duplicative testing to increase classroom instruction time.
Wants baseline safety infrastructure at all schools, including lighting, secure entry systems, and interior classroom locks.
Supports school-based health partnerships and access to accurate, science-based public-health guidance in schools.

md-baltimore-city-2026-boe-atlarge-espos.name: Ashley Ash Esposito
md-baltimore-city-2026-boe-atlarge-espos.bio: Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners at-large member since 2023, chair of its Policy Committee, and a City Schools parent.

positions.stance: Says schools should reflect their neighborhoods and build public trust "through transparency, collaboration, and listening to those closest to the challenges."
Supports breaking stigma and ensuring all students, including those with hidden disabilities or who need extra support, can thrive.
Fights for fair funding, quality instruction, and early supports so all children have the tools to thrive regardless of zip code, background, or ability.

md-baltimore-city-2026-boe-atlarge-flowe.name: Domonique A. Flowers
md-baltimore-city-2026-boe-atlarge-flowe.bio: Former education attorney and substitute teacher; vice chair of the Baltimore City school system's Ethics Panel and former Maryland PTA board member.

positions.stance: Wants improved school safety, better special education compliance, less tardiness and absenteeism, and transparent management of capital and operating budgets.
Supports incentives and training for teachers and staff, wraparound services for families, and greater transparency for parents through community collaborations.
Wants to re-evaluate curriculum, expand tutoring and mentoring, partner with employers, and mandate life-skill classes such as financial literacy.

md-montgomery-2026-boe-atlarge-diaz-bren.name: Brenda M. Diaz
md-montgomery-2026-boe-atlarge-diaz-bren.bio: Social studies teacher with 25 years as an educator, including a decade in Montgomery County Public Schools classrooms; founder of Heart of Joy Learning.

positions.stance: Wants whole books, textbooks, and explicit reading and math instruction in every classroom, with "less technology, more learning" and after-school tutoring.
Supports restoring School Resource Officers, enforcing the Student Code of Conduct, and passing a Teachers' Bill of Rights.
Wants fully equipped schools, content-focused professional development, and curriculum that drives excellence rather than "endless digital platforms."
Says every dollar of MCPS's $3.78 billion budget should be tracked, justified, and tied to student outcomes, with savings redirected to classrooms.
Says parents are the most important stakeholders and should have "a real seat at the table," with neighborhood schools kept as community anchors.

md-montgomery-2026-boe-atlarge-lazo-omar.name: Omar Lazo
md-montgomery-2026-boe-atlarge-lazo-omar.bio: Small business owner, Montgomery College trustee, and chair of the Montgomery County Workforce Development Board.

positions.stance: Will work to reduce class sizes, especially in early grades, increase planning time, and ensure educators have needed resources and staffing.
Committed to strengthening Early College, career technical, IB, and magnet pathways, plus bilingual supports and timely disability services.
Will push for transparent, accessible budgeting, more family engagement, and clear accountability and performance measures.
Advocates fully funded mental health supports, fentanyl prevention education, a consistent safety plan, and training to recognize racism, antisemitism, and Islamophobia.
Will prioritize classroom investments and essential staffing, address aging facilities, and ensure long-term financial sustainability.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-reyes-a.name: Alfredo Reyes
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-reyes-a.bio: Led the coalition behind the Latino Cultural Arts Center and served on Denver's Citizen Oversight Board.

positions.stance: Will direct housing dollars toward homes for families and elders, protect down-payment help and eviction legal aid, and support local hiring.
Supports "a cop for crimes, a responder for crises, treatment instead of a cell."
Wants city dollars going to Denver firms and workers, with every promised project date posted next to the real one.
Says cultural corridors like Santa Fe, Welton, Morrison Road and Little Saigon deserve to be funded like infrastructure.
Supports a shade standard planting trees on the hottest, least-shaded blocks first, and cleaner air where it has been worst.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-traylor.name: Whitney Traylor
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-traylor.bio: Founding partner of Traylor Law Group, trial attorney, and professional mediator.

positions.stance: Proposes a Denver Accountability Council to review major contracts before council votes and wants the auditor's independence protected in law.
Supports allowing more housing types by right near transit, a fee study, and a fast lane for office-to-housing conversions.
Supports housing first while tying shelter and provider contracts to outcomes such as 12-month housing retention, published on a public dashboard.
Wants the Broncos to stay but seeks public reporting of related public spending and enforceable commitments on displacement, transit, and local hiring.
Supports funding wage-theft enforcement, prevailing wage standards on city contracts, and the right to organize.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-walker-.name: Jeff Walker
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-walker-.bio: Former RTD Board of Directors member and Denver Planning Board member; works in compliance at a homeless shelter after 17 years in the utility industry.

positions.stance: Supports a full and permanent ban on new data centers in Denver until technology substantially reduces their environmental and community impacts.
Wants faster residential site plan reviews, more city landbanking of blighted properties for affordable housing, and community-owned housing.
Supports Housing First, more cold weather shelters, and funding STAR so it can operate 24/7.
Wants lower speeds on most streets, more and better sidewalks, and traffic calming identified with neighborhood groups.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-konkle-.name: Gabriel Konkle
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-konkle-.bio: Community organizer and lay leader at Cameron United Methodist Church whose jobs have included finance, tech, and school bus driving.

positions.stance: Wants to rezone exclusionary residential zones, legalize congregational housing, and fine owners leaving rentals vacant six months or longer.
Wants to end Denver's license plate reader contract with Axon, ban data centers in city limits, and restrict AI-powered drones.
Supports free preschool for all 3- and 4-year-olds and wage equity for child care workers.
Supports food forests in parks, no-cost groceries for those in need, and funding for a city-owned grocery store.
Wants police misconduct investigated by a citizen-run body and STAR funding increased using police patrol budget money.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-diaz-cy.name: Cynthia Diaz
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-diaz-cy.bio: Economist and owner of Tonantzin Casa de Café on Santa Fe Drive.

positions.stance: Wants to cut the red tape, fees, and costs the city places on small shops so they can open and stay open.
Backs working families and a livable wage while easing pressure forcing renters and small employers out of the city.
Wants to keep Denver's doors open to unhoused people "with real dignity" and to immigrants.
Wants to protect the independent, family-owned places that make Denver distinctive.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-mejia-m.name: Melissa Adriana Mejía
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-mejia-m.bio: Housing policy advocate, former Denver Planning Board member, and former pastry chef.

positions.stance: Fighting to make child care, groceries, utilities, and transportation affordable, and supports unions and family-sustaining wages.
Supports tenant protections, developing a social housing plan, streamlined permitting, and ensuring "housing first is not housing only."
Supports commercial rental protections and expanding city technical-support programs for local businesses and community organizations.
Wants climate justice and green jobs transition policies that make Denver resilient, lower costs, and improve health.
Supports making Denver's moratorium on new commercial data centers permanent, with narrow exceptions for essential infrastructure.

co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-browne-.name: Jake Browne
co-denver-2026-council-atlarge-b-browne-.bio: Began writing about Denver in 2010 and spent a decade running event operations.

positions.stance: Wants Denver's property tax refund opened to working renters, judged on their own paycheck.
Proposes paying landlords to keep legacy businesses and making landlords pay moving costs when they push steady businesses out at renewal.
Supports a yearly fee on storefronts kept dark for a year, climbing until there is a tenant.
Wants fees automatically reduced the same month whenever the city cuts pickups or services.
"No AI watching us while we drive or while we work"; no surveillance contract vote without a public impact report and council vote.
